ranking.reason: Students with a deadline and a pile of their own PDFs have a frequent, concrete need, and the 12 complaints across 6 apps show the gap, though free general LLMs make the ad less compelling.

A lifter mid-workout who loses sets or sees the watch jump to the wrong exercise feels the failure at the moment of use, which makes a Watch-specific fix a credible ad, though the audience is narrower and Strong- and Hevy-style competitors exist.
Losing a deck or being unable to move decks is a sharp frustration, but the audience is mostly existing flashcard users, and the free incumbent Anki gives them a cheap alternative to a new app.
Fear of losing a lecture recording is real, but the built-in phone recorder and transcription tools already cover much of the need, which weakens the case for tapping an ad for a new app.
Learners pay for language apps and respond to ads, but the job of judging pronunciation accurately is hard to promise credibly, and large incumbents such as Speak, Babbel and Busuu hold the category.
Exact label entry with no AI guessing has a clear niche, but it is the most crowded category, and MyFitnessPal and Cronometer make the ad expensive and the switch from them unlikely.
